disagreements.topic: Value of the foundry option (the main remaining spread in fair value)
disagreements.positions: agent_1 gives foundry plus Mobileye $75B. agent_4 gives $117B, agent_3 $125B and agent_2 $140B. agent_2's figure leans on the Microsoft Maia 2 report, Fortinet and an older Tom's Hardware piece on 'two prospective 14A customers'. agent_3 counts Tesla's Terafab 14A selection.
disagreements.resolution: Partly settled. At Deutsche Bank on 2026-09-02, the CFO said customer talks have moved to 'how much capacity can I get' and that Intel has 'conviction' on external 14A customers. He named no customer and gave no volumes or revenue. The Tesla Terafab tie-up (April 2026) is a technology and manufacturing collaboration with no capital commitment or revenue figure disclosed. Maia 2 on 18A rests on a report, not on a statement from either company. Apple 18A-P is still unconfirmed. A centre near $110-120B is the best-supported figure. agent_1 is a little low given Tesla and the CFO's tone; agent_2 is a little high because two of its supports are reports. Either way the difference is only about +/-$5/share of fair value and does not change the direction against the $120 price.
disagreements.evidence: Bits&Chips on CFO Zinsner at Deutsche Bank (2026-09-02); Yahoo/Simply Wall St and Benzinga on Tesla's Terafab 14A selection (2026-04-22/24); Tom's Hardware Maia 2 headline ('claims report'); TechSpot/Piper Sandler: eight companies evaluating 14A, no commitments (2026-09-25)

disagreements.resolution: The others are better calibrated. A lognormal with the agents' median of about $111 and sigma of 0.65 (realized vol is 72% over 3 months and 76% over 1 year, my own computation) gives about 6.3% at $300. agent_1's bull case ($190 with 38% dispersion) also points to more than 3%. The 5.3% mean is reasonable, so I keep it.

disagreements.topic: Q3 earnings date and what sits inside the 1-month window
disagreements.positions: All agents assume Oct 22 (unconfirmed) with about 85-90% odds inside the window. agent_5 notes that no notice by Oct 2 slightly favours a later print.
disagreements.resolution: Still unconfirmed as of 2026-10-02 03:00 UTC. The latest item on Intel's IR RSS is from Sept 8. The last EDGAR filing is an N-PX on Aug 28: no earnings-date 8-K and no offering filing. The Q2 date was announced 23 days ahead (Jun 30 for Jul 23). The print is still very likely before Oct 31. The company lock-up ends with that release (424B5).

disagreements.topic: Read-through from Micron and IDC into the Q3 print (agent_2)
disagreements.positions: agent_2 cites Micron FQ4 revenue of $54.2B (+379% y/y) as an AI-server positive, and an IDC Q4 PC-unit forecast of -20% as a client negative.
disagreements.resolution: The Micron figure is confirmed by Micron's own FQ4 2026 release: $54.2B revenue, +379% y/y, 87% gross margin. The read-through cuts both ways for Intel. It confirms AI-server demand (good for DCAI), but the same memory-price spike raises PC bill-of-materials costs and supports IDC's weak Q4 PC outlook (bad for CCG). That fits a 1-month median a little below spot.

disagreements.resolution: All three are defensible: the shares are released as Secure Enclave cash arrives, and the cash partly offsets them. The spread is under $2/share. No change.

one_month_reasoning: I keep the forecasters' mean (median about $119). Q3 results are expected around Oct 22 but are still unannounced as of Oct 2, with roughly 85-90% odds of landing inside the window. A beat is likely given server-CPU pricing and Micron's confirmed AI-memory boom. Against that: 8 of the last 11 next-day reactions were negative (mean absolute move about 11%), memory costs weigh on Q4 PC units, and the company lock-up ends with the print, so a new raise becomes possible (none is filed).
confidence_reason: After round 1 the five revised forecasts converged even further (P(>=120) ranges only from 0.436 to 0.463). My searches settled side questions: the Tesla and Maia evidence, the unverified Fitch outlook, the Micron read-through and the unconfirmed earnings date. None of them justifies moving the centre or the tails off the mean.
thesis_break_reason: Below about $70 (about 42% under spot) the market would be valuing the foundry option at close to zero after the $15.6B NCI (agent_2's products-only floor is about $68). That is also about 26% under the $95 August offering and CEO purchase price, and well under the July 2026 low of $81.79, which is where ordinary de-rating stopped. Getting there takes falling estimates: server-CPU pricing reversing, or the 14A anchor decision going against Intel.
key_drivers: Server-CPU shortage and pricing (DCAI +59% y/y in Q2; channel prices up 10-20%), and whether it lasts into 2027 as AMD and Arm capacity arrives. Micron's $54.2B quarter confirms AI-server demand, but memory costs hit PC units

A named, binding 14A anchor customer. Today the evidence is the CFO's 'conviction' (Sept 2), a Tesla Terafab collaboration with no disclosed revenue, report-only Apple 18A-P and Maia 2 deals, and $293M a quarter of external foundry revenue. 14A risk production is set for H2 2027, with HVM in 2028

summary: In round 2 the five forecasters converged further: all now use the corrected share count, the $23B raise and the NCI, with fair values of $94-100 (mean $96) against a $120 price and P(>=120 in a year) of 0.44-0.46. My checks found that no 14A customer is named yet: Tesla's Terafab is a collaboration with no disclosed revenue, Maia 2 and Apple are reports, and a reported Fitch upgrade is unverified. Micron's blowout quarter is confirmed, but it cuts both ways for Intel. None of this justifies moving off the forecasters' mean, which I keep with low confidence: median about $111 in a year and about $119 at end-October. The swing factors are a named 14A anchor (upside) and the Q3 print plus the lock-up ending in late October (two-way event risk).
